goal: Create scripts/chain/evidence.mjs — the impure evidence layer for the B1 gates CLI. It owns exactly two things: (a) the baseline/change-set machinery (a fingerprint-dictionary baseline captured once per slice, and a three-way touched-set union computed against it at gate time), and (b) the validation-command runner (fd-backed spawnSync with synthesized 124/127 classification and a bounded tail read). Every failure mode in this file must fail CLOSED — a rename desync, a -u-collapsed directory, a truncated status buffer, or a swallowed git error must never silently report 'clean'. This is the one file in the initiative whose job is catching what a bypass would look like.
constraints: Follow dispatch.mjs:500-507's gitOutput/gitOk argv-array discipline (execFileSync/spawnSync with an argv array, never a shell string). Do NOT copy dispatch.mjs:1917-1924's gitPorcelain — it swallows every failure to null and uses a bare --porcelain; both are fail-open and wrong here.
conventions.md 2026-08-01 'Prefer structural impossibility to a test assertion, and a whitelist to a blacklist' — the error-code enum is a frozen closed list.

backend-notes.md 2026-08-01 'throw on contract-author error, return violations on data error' and 2026-08-05 'loaders throw on unreadable, unparseable AND well-formed-but-structurally-wrong' — readBaseline throws on a malformed baseline, never degrades to null.

backend-notes.md 2026-08-05 'loader severity splits on asset provenance' — the baseline is instance data this tool itself wrote, so a malformed one is a TAMPER/CORRUPTION signal and throws; an ABSENT one returns null and the caller (gates.mjs) turns that into a hard_fail check.

conventions.md 2026-08-02 'concurrency-unsafe check-then-act is a defect class' — the baseline write is writeFileSync(tmp) + linkSync(tmp, dest); EEXIST is the loser and throws BaselineExistsError. Never existsSync-then-rename.
conventions.md 2026-08-02 'a raw control character written as a string-literal separator makes the source binary to grep' — write '\0' / '\x00' as an escape, never a literal NUL byte.
conventions.md 2026-08-02 'CLI-dependent tests use a repo-local fake-binary fixture' — but git itself is NOT faked here; use real `git init` fixtures (test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs:101 idiom).

backend-notes.md 2026-08-02 'Node never dispatches a signal handler while blocked in spawnSync' — do not register signal handlers around the runner; everything must work on the synchronous return path.
conventions.md 2026-08-01 'no lint or typecheck tooling exists' — plain JS, node builtins only, zero dependencies.
Chain -> cmux is the permitted import direction; never the reverse. scripts/cmux/* must not gain an import of scripts/chain/*.
acceptance_criteria: captureBaseline({ cwd, reason }) returns exactly { anchor_sha, reason, captured_at, dirty } where anchor_sha is `git rev-parse --verify HEAD`, captured_at is an ISO timestamp, and dirty is an object mapping each dirty-or-untracked path to { xy, sha256 }. sha256 is the node:crypto createHash('sha256') hex digest of the file's bytes, or null when the path does not exist on disk at capture time (a staged deletion). anchor_sha is NEVER undefined: an unborn branch (git exits 128) throws EvidenceError with code 'unborn_branch'; any other git failure throws code 'git_unavailable'. Asserted by a real mkdtemp + `git init` fixture with no commit.

The pinned status invocation is exactly `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall`, asserted by a source-text test over scripts/chain/evidence.mjs that requires all four of --no-optional-locks, --porcelain=v1, -z and -uall to appear in one argv array literal. Removing any one of the four fails the test (needle built from fragments per conventions.md 2026-08-08, so the assertion does not match its own source).

parsePorcelainZ(buf) is exported and pure. It decodes the WHOLE buffer as UTF-8 before splitting on '\0' (NUL cannot appear inside valid UTF-8 path bytes), and handles the rename/copy exception: an entry whose XY begins with 'R' or 'C' is `XY<space>TO\0FROM\0` — TO first, reversed vs human `from -> to` display — and yields { xy, path: TO, from: FROM }. A non-rename entry yields { xy, path }. Positives first; then a single-mutation negative where a fixture buffer containing one rename FOLLOWED BY two ordinary entries is parsed — a parser that blindly splits and slices at fixed offsets desyncs and mislabels the following entries, and that must be a failing test with a deepEqual on the exact expected entry list.

A trailing-garbage / truncated status buffer (a final entry with no terminating NUL) throws EvidenceError code 'status_unparseable' — it must NEVER be silently dropped, because a dropped entry is a path that silently reads as untouched.

touchedPaths({ cwd, baseline }) returns { paths: string[] (sorted, deduped, repo-relative POSIX), sources: { committed: string[], dirty: string[], reverted: string[] } } computed as the union of exactly three sources: (1) `git diff --name-only -z <anchor_sha>..HEAD`; (2) the fresh status snapshot's paths, EXCLUDING any path present in baseline.dirty whose current sha256 equals baseline.dirty[path].sha256; (3) every path in baseline.dirty now ABSENT from the fresh status snapshot whose current on-disk sha256 DIFFERS from baseline.dirty[path].sha256. For a rename entry, BOTH the TO and the FROM path are touched.

Each of the three sources is asserted independently against a real git fixture, plus these four named cases, each with its paired positive: (a) a rename (`git mv`) — both paths touched; (b) an untracked file inside a brand-new directory — the full path `newdir/inner.txt` appears, NOT the collapsed `newdir/` (the -uall proof; re-run with -u default in a mutation and assert it regresses); (c) a baseline-dirty file edited then restored to its original bytes — MUST count as touched (source 3, detectable only by content comparison, never by path-membership diffing); (d) a baseline-dirty file left as the user's own untouched edit — MUST NOT count as touched. Each via a real git init/commit/dirty fixture, never a mocked collector.

Named degenerate assertions for touchedPaths, each stated in a comment and each failing the suite: 'always returns []'; 'a diff-only comparison blind to reversions and untracked files' (fails cases b, c); 'path-membership diffing of baseline.dirty against current status' (fails case c); 'returns only the FROM side of a rename' (fails case a).

writeBaselineExclusive(path, baseline) creates the file via writeFileSync(tmp) + linkSync(tmp, dest) and throws EvidenceError code 'baseline_exists' on EEXIST — a second capture NEVER overwrites the first. Asserted. readBaseline(path) returns null iff the file is absent, and throws EvidenceError code 'baseline_malformed' for unreadable, unparseable, or structurally-wrong content (missing/non-string anchor_sha, missing/non-object dirty, a dirty entry lacking xy or lacking an sha256 key) — three separate single-mutation negatives.

runValidationCommand({ cmd, cwd, timeoutMs, logPath }) derives argv by first calling assertValidationCommands([cmd]) from scripts/cmux/resolve.mjs (which internally applies the private assertFirstTokenSafe) and then `cmd.trim().split(/\s+/)` — a lossless exact argv derivation once the command has passed. A RefusalError is caught and returned as { classified: 'refused', code: null, ok: false, note } — never rethrown, never a silent skip. Asserted with a shell-metacharacter command and with a `bash -c ...` command (both refused).

The spawn is exactly `spawnSync(argv[0], argv.slice(1), { cwd, stdio: ['ignore', fd, fd], timeout: timeoutMs, killSignal: 'SIGKILL' })` where fd is a single descriptor from openSync(logPath, 'w') reused for BOTH stdout and stderr, closed in a finally. A source-text test pins that stdio array shape and pins the absence of the string 'pipe' in the stdio literal.

[SUPERSEDED by QA-gate round 1/round 2 fixes — see backend-notes.md] Exit classification is SYNTHESIZED and asserted per branch: res.error?.code === 'ENOENT' -> code 127 (missing_binary); res.error?.code === 'ETIMEDOUT' -> code 124 (timeout) — this is the SOLE timeout predicate (the original elapsed-time heuristic described here was removed after round-1 review found it could misfire on an external signal kill); any other res.error -> classified 'spawn_error', code null, note carries res.error.message (added after round-1 review found non-ENOENT spawn errors were silently discarded); res.status === null with a signal -> 128 + os.constants.signals[res.signal], or classified 'signal_unknown' with code null if the signal name is unmapped; otherwise res.status as-is. A test asserts the ORDER by driving a missing binary and confirming 127 (not 124) even when a timeout is set.

Timeout -> 124 via test/fixtures/slow-command.mjs (holds the event loop past the timeout; the test uses timeoutMs of 300ms so suite growth stays trivial). Missing binary -> 127 via a nonexistent first token. Both asserted with the full RunResult deepEqual on { classified, code } — not just a truthy check.

Huge output: test/fixtures/huge-output.mjs writes >4MB to stdout and stderr. Assert that (i) the call does not throw, (ii) res.error is undefined and the classification is the fixture's real exit code, (iii) the log file on disk contains the full byte count, and (iv) the returned tail is <= 4096 bytes. Comment must state that ENOBUFS is unreachable by construction with an fd (no pipe, no maxBuffer) — that IS the fix — and the code must still carry a defensive branch classifying res.error?.code === 'ENOBUFS' as { classified: 'refused', ok: false } with a note naming it, never as absence of failures. Truncated or absent output on ANY abnormal exit is evidence, never treated as 'no failures'.

The tail read is bounded: openSync(logPath,'r'), statSync size, readSync into a buffer starting at Math.max(0, size - 4000) — never a full-file read (source-text test pins the absence of readFileSync(logPath) in the tail path). Before decoding, leading UTF-8 continuation bytes ((b & 0xC0) === 0x80) are dropped, then the buffer is truncated forward through the first '\n' if one is present. Asserted with a fixture whose 4000-byte boundary lands mid-multi-byte-character: the decoded tail must contain no U+FFFD.

A failing validation command returns ok:false with the captured tail and never throws — a runner error and a test failure are distinguishable outcomes. Multiple failing commands are asserted to be independently runnable with no short-circuiting (gates.mjs owns the loop; this file's contract is that one call never affects another).

EVIDENCE_ERROR_CODES is a frozen exported array; the drift guard asserts BOTH assert.deepEqual(EVIDENCE_ERROR_CODES, [...]) AND assert.ok(Object.isFrozen(EVIDENCE_ERROR_CODES)) (conventions.md 2026-08-08 — deepEqual alone does not pin the freeze).

Review depth: code-reviewer-deep is REQUIRED and this file participates in issue #28's adversarial 3-reviewer panel + test-engineer mutation pass (mutation pass first and alone on the frozen tree). The security-control surface is: agent-controlled command execution (the spawn) and the fail-closed change-set machinery that the protected-path hard_fail depends on.

`node --test test/chain-evidence.test.mjs` green; this file's contribution to suite growth is <= 6s (the git fixtures dominate; keep timeoutMs at 300ms and the huge-output fixture at a single buffered write loop).
